notes: Pavlov speaks its own line-based RCON, not Source RCON: plain TCP on Port from Pavlov/Saved/Config/RconSettings.txt (Password= and Port=, default 9100). The server opens with a password challenge and the client answers with the lowercase hex MD5 of the password; after that each command is sent as a single plain-text line and every reply is a JSON object echoing {"Command":"..."} plus a payload. RCON is off until RconSettings.txt exists. Commands are PascalCase and case-sensitive as the wiki lists them. RefreshList returns {"PlayerList":[{"Username":"...","UniqueId":"..."}]}; ServerInfo returns ServerInfo with MapLabel, GameMode, ServerName, Teams, Team0Score, Team1Score, Round, RoundState, PlayerCount. Identifier is what Pavlov calls the UniqueID - the Steam64 id for PC players and the numeric Oculus/Meta account id for Quest and Pavlov Shack players; both are long digit strings, hence the numeric pattern. Kick, Ban and Unban all take a bare UniqueID and nothing else - there is no reason argument and no ban duration, so {reason} and {duration} are deliberately absent; Ban is permanent and simply appends the id to blacklist.txt, which Unban removes live. There is deliberately NO say/motd entry: the RCON command list has no broadcast or chat command at all (UpdateServerName [Name] changes the server browser name, which is not a broadcast), so RIFT//CTRL should report broadcast as unsupported rather than substituting something. InspectPlayer [UniqueID] gives per-player detail and ModeratorList/Banlist read the mods and blacklist files; Gag [UniqueID] [True/False] is the mute, not a kick. Disagreement between sources: the wiki's worked RCON example uses port 9101 while its own setup page, the Steam guide and both client libraries use 9100 - 9100 is the documented default and 9101 is just that author's server. blacklist.txt path is given as Pavlov/Saved/Config/blacklist.txt by the wiki and the AMP template; the leading directory depends on the install layout (SteamCMD installs under the 622970 or pavlovserver root), so both spellings are listed.
